text:
Ravi: Hi folks  dinner with a partner in Madrid last night, company card declined so I paid on my personal card and the restaurant only gave an EFT payment slip (no itemized receipt). Total €67. Can I still expense it? The slip just shows total and last4.
Maya (People Ops): You can submit but we'll need extra context. Please upload: the EFT slip photo, a photo of the restaurant receipt if available, the calendar invite showing the meeting, and a one-line justification in the expense comment that it was partner dinner and company card declined.
Ravi: No other receipt, server said system was down. I have the partner's confirmation email and my card statement showing the charge.
Maya (People Ops): That should be fine. For meals we also need to categorize tip vs food. If tip isn't broken out, finance will treat the full total as meal and reimburse up to policy limits. If the tip looks excessive (>25%), finance may reach out.
Diego (Finance): Quick note from finance: please mark category = Meals -> "Client meal" and add guest names in the comment. If you want us to exclude a personal item, annotate the line and attach proof. We'll accept partner confirmation + card statement + EFT slip as sufficient for an exception.
Ravi: Uploaded eft_slip.jpg, partner_email.png, card_stmt.pdf. Added guest names and context.
TravelBot: Reminder: policy page https://intranet.redwood.com/travel-expense -> Meals (client entertainment). Use per-diem only if you choose meal allowance instead of actuals.
Maya (People Ops): Thanks Ravi  we'll route to finance and fast-track since you couldn't get a receipt. Diego will confirm once processed.
Diego (Finance): Got it, reviewing now. If we need manager attestation we'll ping. :white_check_mark:
